notes.title: Chains are broken! We are free!
notes.content:
Hi, this is Chris. Main developer of Chains of Fury. Some of you may already know since I posted it on our social media but since our Steam Page is also back in our hands I can post it here as well.

We got our IP Back. We decided to split our ways with the former publisher. It took us a while but it was well worth it. Now we have total control over the project. I will not go into details of our cooperation with the former publisher. The only thing I would like to say that after our successfull Kickstarter campaign which was successful mainly due to efforts of me and my team we got impression that they did not share the same vision of marketing the game as we wanted it to be marketed. We are all adults.  I wish them well. Let them do their thing. We will do ours. 

[h1]What happens now? [/h1]

Lot of stuff is going on at the moment. We are closing the legal stuff and wrapping up the transition. We still need to sort out the transition of the Kickstarter Page. Hopefully we will do iron it out next week.
In the same time we have reinstated the development of the game. After the kickstarter we had to put it on hold but now we are back in action. The game is being redesigned and improved.
All Kickstarter prizes and promises will be fulfilled. The game will probably launch in Early Access sometimes next year but since we are changing and improving a lot of core systems I dont want to risk giving a date. 

For now keep in touch with us.
More to come. 

Chris @ Cobble Games

notes.title: Devlog #8 Core Gameloop. Metroidvania Boomer Shooter
notes.content:
Hey,

Today we want to share our idea for the core gameloop. Since we can destroy most environments in the game, we had to figure out how to funnel the game progress.

Chains of Fury is Metroidvania Boomer Shooter. Following wiki, [i]Metroidvania games feature a large interconnected world map the player can explore, though access to parts of the world is often limited by doors or other obstacles that can only be passed once the player has acquired special items, tools, weapons or abilities within the game. Acquiring such improvements can also aid the player in defeating more difficult enemies and locating shortcuts and secret areas, and often includes retracing one's steps across the map.[/i]

And all this stuff is included in our game.

One could notice this "Scrap Metal +1" pop-up while smashing faces.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/ad041848db5c569a240e8498c7ef62c6bb977758.gif[/img]

In the full game, there will be a special place on each biome operatively named "Safe Zone"
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/4855cddc57b41e8ec29e781d5beec3e9ede171af.png[/img]

This place is important for a few reasons.

First, it resets the level. All mobs killed and all walls destroyed will respawn.
Second, you start in this place after You die. Of course, You are losing all the progress from the run.
Third, this is where You craft Your weapons and armour upgrades that allow You to progress further on the map.
Fourth, You can set Your loadout here.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/7eda26d9581e65f43d7e46d4596867aa10e5d950.png[/img]

You will need two things to get better stuff. Said Scrap Metal and Blueprints
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/356e8ce597f322f61a7842844f33d3ace5b95063.png[/img]

Blueprints unlock craftables, and we pay for them with Scrap Metal that can be used to craft ammunition. New tools open new ways to explore the map.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/90505a768fada43721a26e71d8dc1cf1fd2edd84.gif[/img]

The idea is to have an item required to kill the boss as well. For the first Boss that You may meet in the demo, there is a need to obtain Fire Resistance Armour to survive its large scale lava attack.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/cb33d144379e7957ecbccd2751aa6a07290ff8c3.png[/img]

Meanwhile, we are currently focusing on Main Character movement, game balance, various level design stuff, new enemies and bosses. One can check out current level progress and some bugs we are fighting within the video below:
[previewyoutube=PI_5frKDA9Q;full][/previewyoutube]

And some video showing all stuff above:

[h3]New Features:[/h3]

[b]- Enemy and Exit Markers:[/b]
You will now see a marker if an enemy is nearby. It might change later on to be something temporary. I was thinking to have it activated during fury mode (when you hear the aggressive metal). You will now see mission main objectives. The demo contains now only two of them - kill all enemies and find exit. Later we will add more.

Some of you might have found a pig sitting on a toilet. Places like that will be considered secrets. For now I've added only one such secret marker but later this will be expanded with more such places and interactions. This will also be improved in the future with some dialogues and other stuff. We want to reward you for exploring the level. The level will change after I get all the planned features implemented.

[b]- Walking animation and Weapon Sway[/b]
This was an easy thing to do so I've added a simple weapon sway feature and animation while you walk. It adds a bit of a juice.

- Brawler Pig HP bar was not refreshing. This is fixed now.

- Better AI.

notes.title: Every Story needs a hero
notes.content:
John Carmack once said that a shooter game does not need a deep story. I personally agree that may be true for some First-person shooters. Our game is no different. Common. Let’s face it. We all just want to kick ass and chew bubble gum. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/b0bdaae2fe22d9397c52c17aad51947ecdfdecee.jpg[/img]

We get enough of low blows in real life to get into complex and deep narratives. However, you also might remember why Duke Nukem 3D was so much different from the predecessors - Even though the story was generally not important the Duke himself was so charismatic and outstanding persona that the whole game wouldn't be as fun as if Duke was not present. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/36064736/8eb762705739b71460fb04c936cbbd1d4fc3412a.gif[/img]

This idea seemed to work for all classic games that came out of 3D Realms workshop - Shadow Warrior, Blood are the best examples. Even now in the newer Ion Fury game which is totally awesome, the female protagonist is also very visible. 

Our currently nameless hero, (We still haven't figured out how to name him) is representing the latter - he’s so much there. You can hear him talking, he has his own attitude. Egomaniac, asshole to most, but has his own set of rules:

[b]Rule number one:[/b] Always pay on time. If not he will bash your teeth in.
[b]Rule number two:[/b] You don’t attack innocent people. If you do he will bash your teeth in.
[b]Rule number three: [/b]If a woman attacks you - you don’t bash her teeth in. Throw some chocolate in her direction. This should do the trick.

notes.title: DevLog#1
notes.content:
[h1]Story? Who needs it anyway…[/h1]
[h2]Let’s break sh… stuff.[/h2]


I’ve read in a book called Masters of Doom that John Carmack, father of the old school classic game Doom once said:
"Story in a game is like a story in a porn movie. It's expected to be there, but it's not that important." 

Our game do have a story. Is it that important? Well … no. Let’s face it: You came here not to read complexed dialogues and make meaningful choices. You came here to break stuff. The only meaningful choice of your might be here to pick a proper strategy of clearing the room from aggressive scum. 

Even though you walk through the Valley of the shadow of Death, you should fear no evil...because you are the meanest motherF&@*#@  in the Valley.

The story is simple and straightforward - you want your money back. Others would probably hire a repo man. However here you are your own repo man. So far 100% effective.
Your tools of trade? Mostly fists, sometimes shotgun, if someone is more reluctant then you might consider using a flamethrower.
